1.Nc3 c5 2.d4.strategy: Strikes in the centre at once and offers a pawn trade that brings White's queen out early. It surprises Black, but the queen becomes a target for Black's development, so White gains little more than a sharp start.

1.Nc3 c5 2.Nf3.strategy: Develops the kingside knight and prepares to open the centre with a pawn, keeping White's choices flexible. Black can still stake a claim in the centre at once, so White gets a pleasant but not a commanding game.

1.Nc3 c5 2.Rb1.strategy: Prepares to advance the b-pawn for queenside space without exposing the rook, but it develops nothing and spends a tempo on a rook move. Harmless rather than bad: Black simply uses the time to take the centre.
1.Nc3 c5 2.Rb1.name: Dunst Opening: Twyble Attack

1.Nc3 c5 2.b4.strategy: Offers the b-pawn to open the b-file and drag Black's c-pawn away, but Black takes it with ...cxb4 and attacks the knight with the pawn at the same time. White has no clear compensation for the lost pawn and the lost time.
1.Nc3 c5 2.b4.name: Dunst Opening: Düsseldorf Gambit

1.Nc3 c5 2.d4 cxd4.strategy: Takes the offered pawn. Black trades the c-pawn for White's d-pawn, which removes White's only advanced central pawn and leaves Black a half-open c-file to play on.
